title: Coach: Exploiting Temporal Patterns for All-Resource Oversubscription in Cloud Platforms
problem: Cloud platforms remain significantly underutilized across all resource types (CPU, memory, network, storage) because existing oversubscription approaches target only a single resource (typically CPU), causing the oversubscribed bottleneck to shift to other resources and leaving overall utilization low. Memory oversubscription is especially difficult because memory is non-fungible — physical pages cannot be quickly reassigned between VMs.
motivation: Characterization of over 1 million Azure VMs shows that VMs lasting more than one day consume 96% of resource-hours, many exhibit predictable complementary temporal utilization patterns (daily peaks and valleys), and holistic multi-resource oversubscription can enable ~26% more VMs per server.
method: Coach introduces CoachVM, which splits each resource into a reserved portion (guaranteed allocation) and a shareable portion (drawn from a common pool on demand). For memory, it uses a technique called zNUMA that deprioritizes cold pages so they can be temporarily displaced without disrupting the VM. A machine learning model (random forest regressor) predicts how much of each resource each VM will actually need at different times of day, based on the VM's configuration, time of week, usage history, and customer-specific patterns. The cluster scheduler uses these predictions to pack together VMs with complementary usage patterns—like a daytime-heavy workload with a nighttime-heavy one—and a local monitor prevents resource conflicts by reassigning resources between VMs or migrating a VM to another server when contention occurs.
key_novelty: Coach enables oversubscription of all cloud resources by predicting how each VM's resource needs change throughout the day and colocating VMs with non-overlapping demand peaks, using a split-memory technique (zNUMA) that transparently oversubscribes memory without guest OS modifications.
contributions: Characterization of resource utilization patterns across 1M+ Azure VMs revealing complementary temporal patterns, stranding, and multi-resource bottleneck shifts from CPU-only oversubscription.
CoachVM abstraction partitioning each resource into guaranteed and oversubscribed portions, with PA/VA-backed memory split and zNUMA transparent to guests.
Random forest prediction model for per-VM per-time-window resource utilization used in VM scheduling for temporal pattern exploitation.
Evaluation showing up to ~26% more VMs hosted with minimal performance degradation across real Azure workloads and traces.

metrics.other: ~26% more VMs hosted per server with minimal performance degradation; 4x6hr time windows save ~15% memory and ~20% CPU vs single-lifetime-max allocation

limitations: Memory oversubscription effectiveness depends on the availability of complementary temporal patterns which may not exist for all workload mixes; the approach does not handle GPU or NVMe SSD without hardware ATS/PRI support.
primary_theme: temporal pattern-based holistic cloud VM resource oversubscription
